content.thinking:
I'm mapping out a route from workspace membership through workspace to conversation to message, with workspace membership as the referent entity in single resolution mode, and working out how to phrase the identifying reference back to the message content.

Since there's only one workspace in the seed data, all channels belong to it, so this mostly reduces to identifying by channel plus message content, then retrieving the author's workspace membership record. The actual task seems to involve a state-changing operation on that membership—like promoting the user to admin via the role field in user_teams.

I'm thinking of a scenario: Priya posted a message in core-infra identifying that the memory issue was a CUDA batch size limit, and I want to promote her workspace role to admin as recognition, tracing the route from membership through workspace, conversation, and message with binding checks on the author and workspace match.

For negatives, Lukas and Olena discussed similar diagnostics but neither posted the specific conclusive message, so Priya remains the unique referent — since there's only one workspace, that constraint stays trivial but the route is still meaningful. This is a state-changing task type updating workspace membership.

I'm structuring the roles: target_membership pointing to Priya's row in user_teams for T01WORKSPACE, plus target_message, target_channel, and target_workspace as supporting roles that establish identity, alongside a negative role for Lukas's non-conclusive message.

The actual identifying quote is Priya's message confirming the pprof delta showed the batch size increase hit a hard CUDA memory limit rather than fragmentation — that's the message that satisfies the prompt's condition for promoting her workspace role to admin.

This gives one obligation: target the workspace membership record, mode single, table user_teams, task type state-changing, updating the role attribute. The discovery of the message is folded into identification rather than a separate obligation, so I'll build the access plan using the conversation history to locate that message and then update the role.

But now I realize there's a real problem: scanning the API list, I don't see any endpoint that actually updates a workspace membership's role — no "update user_teams.role" call exists among auth.test, chat.delete, chat.postMessage, chat.update, or the conversations.* endpoints. Without a supported API for that mutation, this state-changing obligation might not be achievable at all, which could make this an unrealized case.

Given that, maybe I should pivot the task type to read-only — instead of changing someone's workspace role, I could frame it as reporting or looking up their current role using users.info, since that data is accessible even without an update endpoint.

  "roles": [
    {"role": "target_membership", "entity": "user_teams", "facts": "U_PRIYA's membership row in T01WORKSPACE currently role=member; this is the record whose role value is being asked about.", "selection": "match", "reason": "Membership of the same user who authored the identifying message, in the workspace containing that message's channel."},
    {"role": "identifying_message", "entity": "messages", "facts": "Message 1706001931.000000 in C_INFRA authored by U_PRIYA: 'Got the pprof delta—it's definitely the batch size increase hitting a hard CUDA memory limit, not fragmentation...'", "selection": "support", "reason": "Uniquely pins the author (and thus the membership) via message content in the channel."},
    {"role": "core_infra_channel", "entity": "channels", "facts": "C_INFRA, channel_name core-infra, team_id T01WORKSPACE, public channel used for infra/on-call/incident discussion.", "selection": "support", "reason": "Provides the conversation node on the route connecting workspace to the identifying message."},
    {"role": "workspace", "entity": "teams", "facts": "T01WORKSPACE, the single workspace containing core-infra and all memberships in this seed.", "selection": "support", "reason": "Provides the workspace node linking the membership to the conversation."},
    {"role": "lukas_negative", "entity": "messages", "facts": "Message 1706001890.000000 in C_INFRA by U_LUKAS speculates about CUDA memory allocator limits and fragmentation but does not confirm the pprof delta result.", "selection": "negative", "reason": "Discusses the same topic and hypothesizes the cause but is not the confirming pprof-delta message; wrong message excluded by exact wording."},

    {"role": "priya_other_channel_negative", "entity": "messages", "facts": "Message 1706028229.000000 in C_GROWTH by U_PRIYA discusses CDN Tokyo latency, unrelated to the CUDA memory conclusion.", "selection": "negative", "reason": "Same author but wrong content and wrong conversation; shows author alone is insufficient without the matching message."}
  ],
  "obligations": [
    {
      "name": "priya_membership_role",
      "description": "Select the single workspace membership (user_teams row) belonging to the user who authored the message in core-infra confirming the batch-size/CUDA-limit root cause, and report that membership's current role.",

      "scope": "the one membership row matching the identified author within the workspace containing core-infra",
      "target_roles": ["target_membership"],
      "candidate_role_sets": null,

      "answer_attributes": [["user_teams.role"]]

  "task_spec": [
    {"line": 1, "text": "Identify who posted the pprof-delta message in core-infra confirming the batch-size/CUDA-limit root cause, and report their current role in the workspace.", "obligations": [1]}

  "scope_exception": null,
  "access_plan": "Use conversations.list/users.conversations to locate the core-infra channel, then conversations.history on that channel to scan messages for the one confirming the pprof-delta/batch-size/CUDA-limit conclusion, identifying its author (U_PRIYA). Then use users.info on that author to read their derived admin/role status backed by the user_teams.role value for the workspace containing core-infra."
